issues.legal_issue: A Gurbhai has no automatic right to succeed to the headship of a religious institution in Punjab without appointment by the fraternity unless a custom of that institution gives the Gurbhai that right.
material_facts: The dispute concerned succession to the headship of a Dera of Sanyasi Sadhus in Punjab.
The claimant relied on his status as a Gurbhai of the deceased Mahant but had not established appointment by the Bhekh or fraternity.
The claimant argued that Punjab law generally entitled a Gurbhai to succeed in the absence of a Chela.
issues.conclusion: There is no general law applicable to religious institutions in Punjab that entitles a Gurbhai to succeed without appointment. The institution is governed by its own custom and practice, and the claimant could not establish title through Gurbhaiship alone without appointment or proof of a contrary custom.
issues.legal_principle: Rattigan's Digest of Customary Law states that there is no general law applicable to religious institutions in Punjab and that each institution is regulated by its own custom and practice; it further states that the office of Mahant is usually elective, though a Mahant may nominate a successor subject to confirmation by the fraternity. The Court relied on Jiwan Das v. Hira Das, A.I.R. 1937 Lah. 311, and referred to Sital Das v. Sant Ram, A.I.R. 1954 S.C. 606, which held in relation to another institution that appointment by the fraternity was required under its usage.

rule.if: religious_headship_succession_claim and institution_in_punjab and claimant_is_gurbhai and claimant_lacks_fraternity_appointment and not proven_custom_allows_succession_without_appointment

predicates.religious_headship_succession_claim: A claimant seeks succession to the headship of a religious institution.
predicates.institution_in_punjab: The religious institution is situated in Punjab.
predicates.claimant_is_gurbhai: The claimant is a Gurbhai of the deceased head of the institution.
predicates.claimant_lacks_fraternity_appointment: The claimant has not established appointment to the headship by the institution's fraternity.
predicates.proven_custom_allows_succession_without_: Evidence establishes a custom of the institution permitting succession without appointment by the fraternity.
predicates.gurbhai_status_alone_does_not_establish_: A claimant's status as a Gurbhai, without appointment or a proven custom allowing succession without appointment, does not establish title to the headship.

issues.definition: When a claimant seeks religious headship in Punjab as a Gurbhai, lacks fraternity appointment, and cannot prove a custom allowing succession without appointment, Gurbhaiship alone does not establish title.

issues.legal_issue: A party claiming succession under a custom that permits a Gurbhai to succeed without appointment must prove that institution-specific custom with adequate evidence.
material_facts: The claimant pleaded that a Gurbhai could succeed to the Dera's headship without appointment by the Bhekh or fraternity.
The evidence consisted of witness statements describing a general practice and referring to examples without sufficient particulars.
The evidence did not establish whether the fraternity had recognized, appointed, or confirmed the successors in the examples cited.
The claimant had not been appointed by the Bhekh or fraternity.
issues.conclusion: The claimant did not establish the alleged custom that a Gurbhai could succeed without appointment by the Bhekh or fraternity.
issues.legal_principle: A party asserting a usage or custom as the basis for succession to a religious office must establish it affirmatively by proper legal evidence. The Court applied the principle stated in Rattigan's Digest of Customary Law that each Punjab religious institution is regulated by its own custom and practice, and referred to Jiwan Das v. Hira Das, A.I.R. 1937 Lah. 311, and Sital Das v. Sant Ram, A.I.R. 1954 S.C. 606.

rule.if: religious_headship_succession_claim and institution_specific_custom_is_asserted and evidence_lacks_particulars and evidence_does_not_show_whether_fraternity_confirmed_precedent_successors

predicates.religious_headship_succession_claim: A claimant seeks succession to the headship of a religious institution.
predicates.institution_specific_custom_is_asserted: The claimant asserts a custom of the institution as the basis for succession.
predicates.evidence_lacks_particulars: The evidence describing the alleged custom or its examples lacks sufficient particulars.
predicates.evidence_does_not_show_whether_fraternit: The evidence does not establish whether the fraternity recognized, appointed, or confirmed the alleged precedent successors.
predicates.asserted_institutional_custom_is_not_pro: The evidence is insufficient to establish the asserted custom of the institution.

issues.definition: When a claimant to religious headship relies on an institution-specific custom but the evidence lacks particulars and does not show whether the fraternity confirmed the cited successors, the custom is not proven.

issues.legal_issue: A plaintiff seeking ejectment must establish the plaintiff's own title and cannot succeed merely because the defendant in possession lacks title.
material_facts: The claimant brought a suit for possession of properties belonging to the Dera on the basis of his asserted title as successor to the Mahant.
The claimant failed to establish title to the headship and the properties.
The claimant argued that others in possession had no title, but the Court assumed that submission in considering the issue.
issues.conclusion: The suit for ejectment was properly dismissed because the claimant failed to establish his own title, notwithstanding the possibility that the defendant in possession lacked title.
issues.legal_principle: In an ejectment suit based on the plaintiff's title, the plaintiff must succeed or fail on the title established by the plaintiff; the defendant's lack of title does not supply the plaintiff's missing title. The Court referred to Mukherjea's Hindu Law of Religious and Charitable Trusts, Second Edition, page 317, which states that a claimant to the office of Mohunt must affirmatively prove the usage on which the claim rests and cannot succeed merely because the defendant is a trespasser.

predicates.ejectment_suit: The proceeding is a suit seeking ejectment or possession of property.
predicates.plaintiff_claims_possession_on_own_title: The plaintiff seeks possession on the basis of the plaintiff's own asserted title.
predicates.plaintiff_fails_to_establish_title: The plaintiff does not prove the title on which the claim for possession rests.
predicates.ejectment_claim_fails_even_if_defendant_: The plaintiff's claim for ejectment fails even if the defendant in possession has no title.

issues.definition: When a plaintiff seeks ejectment on the plaintiff's own title but fails to establish that title, the claim fails even if the defendant lacks title.
